'''Jacob Carl Green''' (born January 21, 1957) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas A&M Aggies football|Texas A&M Aggies]].

Green was an [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] selection in [[1979 College Football All-America Team|1979]] after compiling 134 [[Tackle (football move)|tackles]] and was a then school-record 20 [[quarterback sacks]]. Green's 37 career sacks still rank second in A&M history behind [[Aaron Wallace]]’s 42 career sacks. Green owns school records for career [[fumbles]] caused (12) and season fumbles caused (six in 1978).

Green was a first-round [[Draft (sports)|draft]] pick (10th overall) in the [[1980 NFL draft]] by the [[Seattle Seahawks]]. In his 13-year career in the NFL, Green played 12 seasons for the [[Seattle Seahawks]], as number 79, and one season for the [[San Francisco 49ers]]. Green recorded 97.5 career sacks for the Seahawks (unofficially 115.5; sacks became an official NFL statistic in 1982, Green's third season),<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.seahawks.com/Team/Records.aspx?id=13034 |title=seahawks.com |access-date=2008-02-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071115043141/http://www.seahawks.com/Team/Records.aspx?id=13034 |archive-date=2007-11-15 |url-status=dead }}</ref> a team record and at the time of his retirement good for number three on the all-time sacks leaderboard behind only [[Reggie White]] and [[Lawrence Taylor]].

His jersey number was retired and he was inducted to the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] in 2001. '''Jackie Vernold Shipp''' (born March 19, 1962) is an American [[American football|football]] coach and former player. Shipp was the [[defensive line]] [[Coach (sport)|coach]] for the [[Oklahoma Sooners football]] team until his departure in the 2013 offseason. He had been on the Sooners' coaching staff since the arrival of [[Bob Stoops]] in 1999. He was the defensive line coach at Arizona State from 2013 to 2015,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Trotter |first=Jake |author-link=Jake Trotter |date=February 13, 2013 |title=Bob Stoops of Oklahoma Sooners fires coaches due to poor offensive, defensive line play |url=https://www.espn.com/colleges/oklahoma/football/story/_/id/8944424/bob-stoops-oklahoma-sooners-fires-coaches-due-poor-offensive-defensive-line-play |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> and was the defensive line coach at the University of Missouri for part of the 2016 season.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.stltoday.com/sports/college/mizzou/eye-on-the-tigers/reports-arizona-state-assistant-headed-to-mizzou/article_98f74ba8-d1f0-535e-8377-6de0cdc0a9be.html| title = Mizzou hires Shipp to coach D-line {{!}} Eye on the Tigers {{!}} stltoday.com}}</ref>

Shipp played [[high school football]] in [[Stillwater, Oklahoma]] where he was raised. He played [[college football]] at the [[University of Oklahoma]]. Shipp holds the all-time OU record for [[Tackle (football move)|tackles]] in a single game with 22 and tackles in a single season with 189 (12 games). He is second in career tackles to [[Daryl Hunt]]. He was a second-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-America]] selection in 1983.<ref name="NEA">{{cite news |title=The 1983 NEA All-America team |newspaper=The Republic (Columbus, Ind.) |date=November 30, 1983 |page=16 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/4574799/1983_nea_allamerica_team/|via=Newspapers.com}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref name="CBW">{{cite news |last=Olderman |first=Murray |date=Dec 27, 1983 |title=NEA All-America Team: Rozier Leads Stars |work=The World (Coos Bay, OR)}}</ref>

He played six seasons in the NFL for the [[Miami Dolphins]] from 1984 to 1988 and the [[Los Angeles Raiders]] in 1989. He was selected in the first round of the [[1984 NFL draft]] with the 14th overall pick.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1984 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1984/draft.htm |access-date=October 10, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Jackie Walker''' (born November 3, 1962) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20111122033400/http://databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=WALKEJAC01 Jackie Walker]}}, database Football. Accessed May 23, 2009.</ref> He was the 28th player selected in the [[1986 NFL draft]], the first player drafted in the second round of a year in which there were only 27 first-round picks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1986 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1986/draft.htm |access-date=2023-10-02 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> His selection was controversial, as he did not score particularly well in the pre-draft combines, and there were more-heralded linebackers still on the board.<ref>Steele, David. "Selection of Walker a surprise". St. Petersburg Evening Independent. April 30, 1986</ref><ref>Flanagan, Mike. "Bucs' picks make a case for defense". St. Petersburg Evening Independent. April 30, 1986</ref> Walker attended [[Carroll High School (Monroe, Louisiana)|Carroll High School]] in [[Monroe, Louisiana]].  He was a latecomer to organized sports, not playing football until high school coaches and his older brother convinced him to join the team in his senior year of high school.  A quick and aggressive player, he was a starter all four years at [[Jackson State University]], where he also played power forward for the basketball team. In his senior year, he led the team with 131 tackles, was named to two All-American teams, and was named [[Southwestern Athletic Conference]] Defensive Player of the Year.<ref>Fry, Darrell. "Walker a linebacker with lots of punch". St. Petersburg Times. June 11, 1986</ref> While the Buccaneers staff were impressed with his raw talent and saw him as a potential [[Ted Hendricks]]-type player, the fans were critical of the selection of a player with so little training and experience.<ref>Flanagan, Mike. "Bucs' Jackie Walker is still catching up". St. Petersburg Evening Independent. May 9, 1986</ref> Walker started only nine games for the Buccaneers, all in [[1987 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|1987]].<ref>[http://www.buccaneers.com/draft/draftmain.aspx?full=true&newsid=7033], buccaneers.com. Accessed May 23, 2009</ref> Although popular with teammates and a standout on special teams, he never worked his way into the regular lineup. Buccaneers coach [[Ray Perkins (wide receiver)|Ray Perkins]] at one point toyed with the idea of taking advantage of his athleticism by converting him to tight end, but dropped the idea due to lack of interest from Walker. When [[Plan B free agency]] began in 1989, Walker was one of the players allowed to leave.<ref>Leone, Tim. "Tampa Bay's lists have surprises". The Lakeland Ledger. February 3, 1989</ref><ref>Harris, John. "Walker apparently won't switch to TE". St. Petersburg Times. July 15, 1988</ref> He was signed by the [[New York Jets]] in [[1989 NFL season|1989]] after being left unprotected by the Buccaneers, but was cut from the Jets in training camp.<ref>"Jets Sign Linebacker". The New York Times. March 24, 1989</ref><ref>Eskenazi, Gerald. "Jets Have a Youthful Look". The New York Times. September 4, 1989</ref> He later played for the [[Cincinnati Rockers]], [[Florida Bobcats|Miami Hooters]], and [[Orlando Predators]] of the [[Arena Football League (1987–2008)|Arena Football League]].<ref>[http://www.arenafan.com/players/Jackie_Walker-1642/] Arenafan.com. Accessed May 23, 2008.</ref>
